name: sim_cvc5_dialogue_game_lorenzen_constraint
description: Lorenzen dialogue games: winning condition via cvc5 SMT, strategy tree depth via sympy

pytorch.reason: pytorch not needed; pure symbolic/algebraic computation via cvc5 and sympy

pyg.reason: PyG message passing not needed; dialogue games handled via SMT solver

z3.reason: z3 not needed; cvc5 handles all SMT constraint proofs in this sim

cvc5.reason: cvc5 SMT solver: load_bearing proof of winning condition constraints

sympy.reason: sympy: supportive symbolic algebra for strategy tree depth formulas

clifford.reason: Clifford algebra not needed; dialogue logic constraints only

geomstats.reason: geomstats not needed; no differential geometry in this sim

e3nn.reason: e3nn not needed; no SO(3) equivariance required

rustworkx.reason: rustworkx not needed; no graph structure in this sim

xgi.reason: xgi not needed; pairwise interactions only

toponetx.reason: toponetx not needed; standard algebraic ops sufficient

gudhi.reason: gudhi not needed; no persistent homology in this sim

test_simple_dialogue_P_wins.interpretation: Dialogue where P answers all attacks and has last move is winning

test_multiple_attacks_all_answered.interpretation: Dialogue with 3 attacks, all answered by P, P has last move

test_unanswered_attack.interpretation: P cannot win with unanswered O-attacks (UNSAT)

test_O_has_last_move.interpretation: P cannot win if O has last move (UNSAT)

test_minimal_dialogue.interpretation: Thesis with no attacks is a valid winning dialogue

test_maximal_dialogue.interpretation: Dialogue with 10 attacks, all answered, is winning
